standard_prerequisites.name: Negation as a function type
standard_prerequisites.statement:
Negation is not a primitive: 
eg A is by definition the function type A 	o \emptyt, so a proof of 
eg
eg A is a function (A 	o \emptyt) 	o \emptyt.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the definition the proof starts from (source line 182).

standard_prerequisites.name: Univalence and transport along a path of types
standard_prerequisites.statement: A path p : A = B of types induces an equivalence of the types, and dependent functions act on paths: apd f p transports f(A) along the family.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof applies the action on paths of a putative f at the path ua(e) of Bool with itself (source lines 190-196).

standard_prerequisites.name: Fixed-point-free autoequivalence of the booleans
standard_prerequisites.statement: The swap e : Bool \simeq Bool sending true to false and false to true has no fixed point.
standard_prerequisites.use: The contradiction is extracted by applying a fixed-point equation to e (source line 216).

standard_prerequisites.name: Function extensionality on a negated type
standard_prerequisites.statement:
Any two elements of 
eg
eg Bool are equal, because 
eg
eg Bool is a function type into \emptyt and \emptyt is a proposition.
standard_prerequisites.use: It collapses the transported argument to the original one (source lines 200-204).

core_obligations: Assume f : \prd{A:\UU} (\neg\neg A \to A) and derive an element of \emptyt (source lines 182-185).

Form the path p \defeq \ua(e) for the fixed-point-free swap of Bool and apply the dependent action on paths of f at p, obtaining the transported value of f(Bool) equals f(Bool) (source lines 188-196).

Rewrite the transported function by the transport rule for arrow types (eq:transport-arrow) and use the collapse of 
eg
eg Bool by function extensionality to get e(f(Bool)(u)) = f(Bool)(u) for an arbitrary u : 
eg
eg Bool (source lines 197-209).
Prove \prd{x:\Bool} \neg(e(x)=x) by case analysis on the two elements of Bool and apply it to f(Bool)(u) to obtain an element of \emptyt (source lines 210-216).

proof_roadmap.step: Unfold the definition of negation and assume the putative f by way of contradiction.
Feed the fixed-point-free swap into f through the action on paths at ua(e).
Transport along the arrow-type rule and collapse the argument with function extensionality.
Show the swap has no fixed point and apply that to the resulting fixed point.

difficulty_reason:
Counted unit is the author's labelled theorem at source lines 177-180 (book Theorem 3.2.2): it is not the case that every A : \UU satisfies 
eg
eg A 	o A. The statement records only a negative existence claim, while the proof (source lines 181-221) has to build the counterexample from the univalence machinery: it assumes f : \prd{A} (
eg
eg A 	o A), forms the path ua(e) of Bool with itself given by the fixed-point-free swap, applies the dependent action on paths of f at that path, rewrites the result through the transport rule for arrow types (eq:transport-arrow), collapses the transported argument by function extensionality on 
eg
eg Bool, and finally converts the transport along ua(e) in the family A \mapsto A into an application of e, whose fixed-point-freeness is checked by case analysis on Bool. None of these steps is determined by the statement, and no purely propositional manipulation of 
eg
eg A can produce the contradiction.
